evidence.claim: Karat Packaging is listed on NASDAQ under ticker KRT and is described as a specialty distributor and manufacturer of disposable foodservice products used by national and regional restaurants and foodservice settings in the United States.

Karat's product disclosure includes food and take-out containers, bags, tableware, cups, lids, cutlery, straws, specialty beverage ingredients, equipment, gloves, eco-friendly products, customized solutions, printing, and logistics services.
Karat Packaging's market capitalization was reported around $568 million to $600 million in June 2026, placing it in the preferred underfollowed small-cap range for this pass.
Ranpak provides protective packaging solutions, packaging automation, and cold-chain products used to insulate temperature-controlled goods during transport.
Ranpak's market capitalization was reported around $584 million to $645 million in June 2026, within the preferred $300 million to $1 billion underfollowed hunting band.

Graphic Packaging names quick-service restaurant customers including Chick-fil-A, McDonald's, Wendy's, Panda Express, Dairy Queen, Chipotle, Panera, and KFC, while also disclosing that no single customer represented 10% or more of net sales in 2025, 2024, or 2023.

evidence.claim: Avery offers tamper-proof labels for food safety, to-go items, deliveries, and takeout containers; the labels use security slits that break when removed and cannot be reapplied.

Avery Dennison's Optica Intelligent Labeling solution targets restaurants with digital IDs, product traceability, food safety and compliance, recall support, freshness, shipment verification, and labor efficiency.
Avery Dennison's market capitalization was reported at about $12.3 billion to $12.5 billion in June 2026, so it is included only as a large-cap reference for labeling and traceability tools.

memory_update.text: KRT should remain the primary underfollowed candidate for the delivery-packaging node because it has direct disclosed foodservice, restaurant, takeout-container, bag, cup, lid, cutlery, glove, printing, and logistics exposure.

PACK is a second-order cold-chain packaging hypothesis, not yet a proven restaurant-delivery supplier; keep only if later evidence shows material foodservice, prepared-meal, grocery, or restaurant-distributor exposure.

GPK provides a scaled reference benchmark for paperboard foodservice cups, trays, containers, and QSR customer relationships; useful for comparing scale, sustainability compliance, and customer lock-in against smaller suppliers.
AVY maps to the tamper-evident label and intelligent food-traceability subnode rather than disposable packaging; verify materiality before treating it as a restaurant theme exposure.

Need a follow-up pass on private or recently delisted foodservice-packaging suppliers such as Dart/Solo, Genpak, Novolex/Pactiv, Veritiv, and distributor private-label packaging programs, because they may define the competitive landscape even if not directly investable.

node: Delivery packaging, cold-chain consumables, and last-mile operating supplies
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the universe around restaurant delivery packaging and related operating consumables. The best underfollowed fit found is Karat Packaging because its disclosed product set is directly tied to disposable foodservice products, takeout containers, bags, cups, lids, cutlery, gloves, logistics, and restaurant customers. Ranpak is a weaker but potentially interesting second-order cold-chain and paper-protection hypothesis because its cold-chain packaging is disclosed, but restaurant delivery exposure needs verification. Graphic Packaging is a larger reference/bridge name with explicit quick-service restaurant customers and foodservice cups, trays, and containers. Avery Dennison is a large-cap niche-tool reference for tamper-evident labels and restaurant traceability/food-safety labeling rather than a pure packaging beta.
